classification.difficultyReason: Find an exact triangle area, then express it as the sum of two smaller triangle areas to determine an unknown length.

content.prompt: Find the exact value of the area of $\triangle KLM$ and hence find the exact value of $x$.

spec.description: Unshaded triangle KLM with horizontal base LM. N lies between K and M, and LN divides the angle at L into two labelled 30-degree angles. Ordinary lines and labels use black.
spec.mathematics: KL=3, LM=6, angle KLN=30 degrees, angle NLM=30 degrees, LN=x. Coordinates are derived from these relationships; no coordinate values or additional measurements are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: All edges, names, angle labels and supplied lengths are permanent question givens. The numerical value of x is absent.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{aligned}
\angle KLM&=30^{\circ}+30^{\circ}\\
&=60^{\circ}\\
\operatorname{Area}(\triangle KLM)&=\frac12(3)(6)\sin60^{\circ}\\
&=\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}.
\end{aligned}$$
Since $N$ lies on $KM$, the two smaller triangle areas add to the whole triangle area.
$$\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{Area}(\triangle KLN)+\operatorname{Area}(\triangle NLM)&=\operatorname{Area}(\triangle KLM)\\
\frac12(3)x\sin30^{\circ}+\frac12(6)x\sin30^{\circ}&=\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}\\
\frac34x+\frac32x&=\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}\\
\frac{9x}{4}&=\frac{9\sqrt3}{2}\\
x&=2\sqrt3.
\end{aligned}$$

teachingContext.methodNote: The supplied source working uses the area rule with the combined 60-degree angle, then adds the areas of triangles KLN and NLM using their 30-degree included angles. Preserve this method rather than substituting an angle-bisector shortcut.
